statement: Assume Assumption 1.1, the parameter hierarchy (3.1)– (3.2), and a common bound on the Gaussian Bol norms of all birth inputs. For sufficiently large fixed L and sufficiently small ϵ, the following hold. (a) For admissible dependent histories with prescribed labeled roots, fixed b, and complexity ρ, the sum of their normalized positive integrals is at most Cb τb/10 ϵc∗ρ | log ϵ|C∗ρ . (3.10) The sum includes the graph enumeration and the admissible indicator restrictions; a bounded observable multiplier costs its supremum. The birth inputs need not equal the approximate density constructed in the source, but must satisfy its common Gaussian Bol envelope. (b) Suppose the independent input g in slab i satisfies ∥g − f(i−1)τ ∥Bol,βi−1 ≤ ϵθi−1 . (3.11) Let Tϵ i[g] be the leading signed sum just defined. Then ∥Tϵ i[g] − fiτ ∥Bol,βi ≤ 1 2ϵθi . (3.12) In the fixed-top-endpoint norm Bol, ~ βi, the summed absolute contributions of cyclic members of Ti, members of T err i , and tree members of Ti with at least Λi/3 lines are o(ϵθi ). Fixed powers of the cutoffs, arising from a bounded number of selected edge positions, can be included. A fixed exponential factor per atom can also be included by choosing L sufficiently large. Part (b) also holds uniformly when the final slab stops at any 0 ≤ σ ≤ τ. With the same cutoffs and exponent budgets, write Tϵ i,σ for its signed tree sum. Then sup 0≤σ≤τ ∥Tϵ i,σ[g] − f(i−1)τ+σ∥Bol,βi ≤ 1 2ϵθi , (3.13) and the positive error classes obey the same full-τ upper majorants uniformly in σ. At σ = 0 the map is the identity and its contact error classes vanish. The assertion in (b) is about the specified complete signed tree sum and positive error classes. Identifying a different one-root operator with that sum up to those errors requires a separate combinatorial argument.
